info.title: OpenAsy Analytics API
info.summary: How people use your websites, from one script tag, kept in the install.
info.description:
Every screen of analytics uses this API, and so can your scripts (ADR 0014). Within `/api/v1` changes are additive only; anything removed is deprecated first (ADR 0024). Errors use Problem Details (RFC 9457).

Pages send what happened with `/api/v1/collect`, from the site's script at `/s/<site>.js`. Sites are set in the sites file, never through the API. Everything else takes the session of a signed-in person or an API token, and each operation names the role it needs (`x-openasy-role`: viewer, editor, admin; ADR 0003).

Sign-in, members and API tokens are under `/api/v1/auth`, provided by [@openasy/auth](https://github.com/openasy/auth#routes).

post.summary: Send what happened on a page
post.description: What the script sends, as text/plain so navigator.sendBeacon needs no preflight; JSON is taken too. From a page, the Origin must be one of the site's domains, and the answer carries it back in Access-Control-Allow-Origin. From a site's servers, send the key its serverKey names in x-analytics-key instead. Batches from crawlers are acknowledged and dropped. The body may be gzipped, up to 64 KiB unpacked.

202.description: Taken. Events from another origin or an ignored path are dropped and counted.

get.description: The script tag of a site: `<script defer src=".../s/shop.js"></script>`. It carries the site's settings from the file and may be cached for five minutes. /s/replay.js is the replay recorder and /s/heatmap.js the heatmap overlay; the site's script loads them when they are needed.

post.summary: Send a chunk of a visit's replay
post.description: What replay.js sends: a gzipped JSON array of rrweb events as the body, as text/plain so the page needs no preflight, with the visit's ids in the query. Taken only from the site's domains, for sites with replays in the sites file. Emails, tokens and keys in it are masked before it is kept. Up to 2 MiB gzipped, 24 MiB unpacked, and 32 MiB a visit.

202.description: Taken, or dropped when the visit's replay is full or another visitor's.

session.name: __Host-openasy-session
session.description: The browser session after signing in (`openasy-session` when analytics runs on plain http://localhost). Requests that change something must come from the analytics origin.

apiToken.description: An API token created under Settings → API tokens (`oa_analytics_...`): one role, always an expiry (ADR 0003).

adminToken.description: Only when analytics is started by its tests or a local script: one shared token with the admin role. A production install does not have it.

serverKey.name: x-analytics-key
serverKey.description: The value of the environment variable a site's serverKey names, for events sent from the site's servers.

Problem.description: An error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

id.description: The product, as OpenAsy names it.

url.description: The address people open it at.

BatchEvent.description: One thing that happened on a page. Form values are not part of it.

type.description: form: a form field was entered first (start), left, or the form was sent (submit) or given up (abandon); its value is never part of it. forget deletes everything kept about the visitor: the page withdrew consent.

at.description: Milliseconds since 1970 on the page's clock; trusted within a day of the server's.

url.description: The page's address. Required but for forget. Only utm_* and the site's own query parameters are kept.

referrer.description: pageview: where the visitor came from.

target.description: click: a selector that finds the element again, for the heatmap.

text.description: click: what the element says, up to 80 characters.

duration.description: leave: milliseconds on the page. form: milliseconds in the field.

scroll.description: leave: how far down the page was read, in percent.

x.description: click: where in the element, in thousandths of its width.

y.description: click: where in the element, in thousandths of its height.

form.description: form: the form's selector, such as form#signup.

field.description: form: the field's name or id. One named like a card number or a password is kept as its kind, such as (password).

kind.description: form: the field's kind: text, email, password, tel, number, url, search, date, select, textarea, checkbox, radio, file or other.

filled.description: form leave: whether the field had anything in it, never what.

again.description: form leave: whether the field was entered before in this form.

site.description: The site's name in the sites file.

visitor.description: Random, made by the script and kept in the site's localStorage.

session.description: Random, made by the script; a visit ends after 30 minutes without activity.

user.description: The site's own opaque id for the person. Email addresses and phone numbers are refused.

ConfigFile.description: The sites file and whether it is applied; null before it was first read.

error.description: Why the file on disk is not applied; the last good version stays in use.

script.description: The address of the site's script tag.

forms.description: Whether the script reports form fields entered and left.

live.description: Visitors active in the last five minutes.

replay.description: Whether the visit has a replay.

rage.description: Rage clicks: three clicks or more on the same element within a second.

recording.description: The visit's replay as rrweb events; empty without one.

visits.description: Visits that reached the step, having done every step before it in order.

median.description: Median seconds from the step before; null for the first.

enabled.description: Whether the site has forms: true in the sites file.

starts.description: Visits that entered a field of it.

median.description: Median seconds from the first field to sending it.

left.description: Visits that gave the form up at this field.

again.description: Share of the visits that reached it and came back to it.

url.description: The page on the site's first domain, for the frame.

points.description: Clicks by element and by cell of a 20 by 20 grid over it, x and y at the cell's centre in thousandths.

scroll.description: The share of views read to each tenth of the page.
